title: Repurposing rifaximin against Klebsiella pneumoniae via targeting of transcription anti-termination protein RfaH for novel antimicrobial development.
authors: Ashraf, Anam; Choudhury, Arunabh; Khan, Mohammad Ali; Alotaibi, Bader S; Noor, Saba; Hassan, Md Imtaiyaz
one_liner_zh: 该文通过分子对接和MD模拟研究利福昔明靶向Klebsiella pneumoniae转录抗终止蛋白RfaH的抑制机制，虽涉及蛋白-核酸相关转录调控蛋白，但核心是药物-蛋白互作而非TF-DNA结合，方法可迁移但对象偏离。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Multidrug-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae (MDR-KP) has become a critical global health threat, challenging the management of infectious diseases. Anti-termination protein RfaH is crucial in promoting virulence across Gram-negative pathogens, including Klebsiella pneumoniae (KP). RfaH is a key anti-terminator protein involved in transcription regulation that directly interacts with RNA polymerase and ribosomes, activating operons associated with capsule, cell wall, and pilus biosynthesis. METHODS: This study aimed to investigate the repurposing potential of rifaximin, a well-established antibiotic, against (KP) by targeting RfaH. We employed an integrated computational approach of molecular docking and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to obtain atomistic insights into the binding mechanism of rifaximin with RfaH. The computational findings were further validated through experimental assays, including fluorescence-based binding studies, antibacterial activity tests, and evaluation of capsule production in KP. RESULTS: Fluorescence studies showed excellent binding affinity between rifaximin and RfaH (Ka = 7.38 x 10(6) M(-1)). Notably, rifaximin treatment results in a significant reduction in capsule production in KP compared to untreated controls, highlighting its inhibitory effect on RfaH activity. The minimum inhibitory concentration for Rifaximin was 100 muM, and a minimum bactericidal concentration of 200 muM was determined against KP (ATCC 700603 strain). Docking and MD simulation studies provided detailed atomic insights into the Rifaximin binding to RfaH and structural dynamics of the RfaH-Rifaximin complex. CONCLUSIONS: These multifaceted findings collectively investigated the potential of rifaximin as a repurposed antibiotic for the treatment of KP. Finally, a strong interaction of RfaH with rifaximin and subsequent inhibition of the growth of KP provides a novel avenue for antimicrobial development to address the persistent global challenge of antibiotic-resistant infections.
abstract_zh: 背景：多重耐药肺炎克雷伯菌（MDR-KP）已成为全球重大健康威胁，对感染性疾病的管理构成挑战。抗终止蛋白RfaH在促进包括肺炎克雷伯菌（KP）在内的革兰阴性病原体毒力中起关键作用。RfaH是一种关键的抗终止蛋白，参与转录调控，直接与RNA聚合酶和核糖体相互作用，激活与荚膜、细胞壁和菌毛生物合成相关的操纵子。方法：本研究旨在探讨利福昔明（一种成熟抗生素）通过靶向RfaH对KP的再利用潜力。我们采用分子对接和分子动力学（molecular dynamics）模拟的综合计算方法，获得利福昔明与RfaH结合机制的原子级见解。计算结果通过实验测定进一步验证，包括基于荧光的结合研究、抗菌活性测试以及KP荚膜产生的评估。结果：荧光研究显示利福昔明与RfaH之间具有优异的结合亲和力（Ka = 7.38 x 10(6) M(-1)）。值得注意的是，与未处理对照组相比，利福昔明处理显著减少了KP的荚膜产生，突显了其对RfaH活性的抑制作用。利福昔明对KP（ATCC 700603菌株）的最低抑菌浓度为100 μM，最低杀菌浓度为200 μM。对接和MD模拟研究提供了利福昔明与RfaH结合及RfaH-利福昔明复合物结构动力学的详细原子见解。结论：这些多方面发现共同探讨了利福昔明作为治疗KP的再利用抗生素的潜力。最后，RfaH与利福昔明的强相互作用及随后对KP生长的抑制，为应对抗生素耐药感染的持续全球挑战提供了抗菌药物开发的新途径。
